compsNote: 1 of the 3 competitors are within 1 km. Near-twins come first: up to two condos within 1.5 km with a similar number of homes (half to double) completed in 2016 or later. Then every suitable condo within 1 km (same tenure, completed 2011 or later first), widening to 2 km and 3 km only if fewer than 3; executive condos are left out. Resale prices are URA medians for the last 6 months where there were at least 5 resales, otherwise the last 12 months. Condos launched before June 2023 measured their areas under the old rules (including air-con ledges), so their psf is raised 5% to compare like for like.
priceDecide: Like for like by size: for each unit type we take each resale competitor's average psf for units within about 15% of that size (last 6 months, or 12 or 24 if too few). Where a competitor has too few resales of a size, that size is estimated from its own nearest size, so every unit type is judged against the same competitors. Each is raised by a new-launch premium that rises with each competitor's age (40% to 50% here): launches selling now in the OCR charge about 9% over a just-completed resale and about 2.6 points more for each year of its age (30 launches against 107 of their resale competitors, this one and the 6 most extreme pairs left out). Buy at or below = the average of the competitors' new-launch equivalents for that size (a launch nearby from the last 2 years counts for half); walk away above = 5% more. 2-bed: buy at or below $2,360, walk away above $2,480, this project about $2,506 psf; 3-bed: buy at or below $2,220, walk away above $2,330, this project about $2,505 psf; 4-bed: buy at or below $2,140, walk away above $2,250, this project about $2,503 psf. This project's price by unit type follows the developer's launch 'from' prices. No developer floor can be worked out: the developers already owned the land.

HDB resale prices rose 4.2% a year over the past 10 years, so upgraders' capital usually grows too. Singaporean HDB owners who buy before selling pay 20% Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty upfront and get it back only if they sell the flat within 6 months (IRAS).

Score out of 10, same rules for every plan: start at 4; +1 regular shape, dumbbell, kitchen that can be closed off, kitchen or yard window, AC ledge and planter under 5%, store or shelter or utility room; −1 long corridor, ledge and planter 10% or more, balcony over 12%. supply.ring: outer suburbs (11 km or more from the CBD)
concerns: Will too many new condos nearby hurt my price?

Besides this project's own 113 homes, about 895 new homes within 2 km launch within about 2 years of it (Bedok Rise (GLS), Vela Bay); the condo resale market within 2 km handles about 368 resales a year. Our test of 33 condos completed 2016 to 2022 in the outer suburbs (11 km or more from the CBD): those with more than 1,817 other new homes completing within 2 km and 2 years grew 4.0% a year over the past 4 years, against 4.3% for those with fewer (URA caveats). Supply nearby is not a big concern here.
The developer paid more for the land. Am I paying more?

Across 16 launches since 2023, launch prices rose roughly dollar for dollar with break-even (about $103 per $100), so developers kept a similar dollar margin while their percentage margin shrank (22% above break-even on land of $1,200 psf ppr or more, 31% on cheaper land). Part of that is location: dearer land is usually where homes sell for more anyway. So a high bid does show up in prices, but only as far as buyers will pay against nearby homes. The test that protects you is the price against same-size competitors: our buy-at and walk-away prices.
Will the developer cut prices later?
95% sold so far. Developers must sell every unit within 5 years of buying the land or repay most of a 40% stamp duty (IRAS); with most units sold, there is little pressure to cut prices.
Should I wait for the next launch nearby?

The next launch nearby, Bedok Rise (GLS), is likely at about $2,300 to $2,700 psf, close to this project's 3-bed. A cheaper neighbour later could cap this project's resale price; compare both before committing.

Islandwide, about 18,296 private homes complete in 2027 and 2028 and 15,810 homes in the pipeline were still unsold at mid-2026 (URA). That is enough to keep price growth moderate, but local supply and the local buyer pool matter more for your resale.
